prompt: An attacker intercepts an encrypted database backup on a public network. Because the attacker does not have the private key, they cannot read any information. Which pillar of the CIA triad successfully held firm?
options: Availability
Confidentiality
Integrity
Non-repudiation
explanation: Confidentiality ensures that unauthorized parties cannot access or decipher secret data.

prompt: A rogue insider alters the account balance records in a bank database without authorization. Which pillar of the CIA triad has been directly violated?
options: Confidentiality
Integrity
Availability
Scalability
explanation: Integrity guarantees that data has not been modified, forged, or deleted in an unauthorized manner.

prompt: According to the Cyber Kill Chain model, which of the following represent stages prior to the attacker achieving 'Actions on Objectives'? (Select all that apply)
options: Reconnaissance
Delivery
Command & Control (C2)
Permanent Server Decommissioning
explanation: Reconnaissance, Weaponization, Delivery, Exploitation, Installation, and Command & Control all precede the final Actions on Objectives phase.

prompt: Why is 'Security through Obscurity' (e.g., merely changing a port number) considered insufficient on its own?
options: Because changing port numbers consumes significantly more bandwidth.
Because automated port scanners can systematically sweep all 65,535 ports and fingerprint running services in minutes.
Because operating systems automatically shut down when non-standard ports are used.
Because encryption only works on port 443.
explanation: Obscurity slows down automated script-kiddie noise slightly, but port scanners and banner grabbers discover services quickly regardless of port numbers.

prompt: A financial company hosts an internal wiki server accessible only on their private corporate Wi-Fi. An employee connects to the Wi-Fi on an infected laptop, which immediately connects to the wiki and extracts unencrypted payroll files. What structural security failure occurred?
scenarioContext: Network Topology: Single Flat Subnet | Authentication: Implicit Trust for Local IP range
options: Lack of Zero Trust: The network operated on the outdated 'Castle & Moat' model, implicitly trusting any device once inside the perimeter.
The Wi-Fi was broadcasting an 802.11ac signal instead of 802.11ax.
The server used Python instead of C++ for backend scripting.
The database had too many indexes enabled.
explanation: Zero Trust mandates that internal network presence alone never grants access. Every device and session must be authenticated and authorized under least privilege.

prompt: What is the primary objective of an egress filter on an enterprise edge firewall?
options: To prevent internal users from receiving incoming web traffic.
To restrict and monitor outbound network traffic originating from internal hosts to the public internet.
To encrypt local hard drives automatically during peak hours.
To increase maximum broadband upload speeds.
explanation: Egress filtering blocks compromised internal hosts from phoning home to attacker Command & Control (C2) servers or exfiltrating stolen data.

prompt: What does the principle of 'Defense-in-Depth' advocate?
options: Relying entirely on a single ultra-powerful military-grade firewall.
Deploying multiple overlapping security controls (MFA, firewalls, EDR, least privilege) so that if one fails, others stop the breach.
Disabling all outbound internet access across all corporate laptops.
Encrypting only the top 10% most expensive database tables.
explanation: Defense-in-depth ensures resilient redundancy: no single control failure leads to total system compromise.

prompt: During an incident, a SOC team detects suspicious outbound DNS queries transmitting base64-encoded strings to an unknown foreign domain every 30 seconds. In which stage of the Cyber Kill Chain is the attacker operating?
scenarioContext: Outbound Traffic: DNS TXT Queries | Frequency: Every 30s | Destination: dynamic-c2-node.xyz
options: Reconnaissance
Command & Control (C2) / Exfiltration
Initial Weaponization
Network Subnetting
explanation: Periodic beaconing and encoded data transfers over DNS tunneling are classic hallmarks of Command & Control channels and data exfiltration.
